correctness.rationale: With per-edge unit jump rates and killing at the two sites, the positive definite killed Laplacian yields the vector of lifetimes x by solving (L+D)x=1. If t and u are the trap rates times their local lifetimes, then t+u=n. Applying L^+ gives x=T*1-t L^+ e_a-u L^+ e_b for the uniform mean over all sites. Constant diagonal g and off-diagonal g-d give (1/kappa_a+d)t=(1/kappa_b+d)u, hence T/n=g+(1-d^2 P)/(K+2dP). For distinct sites d=R_eff/2>0; the derivative with respect to P is strictly negative at fixed K. AM–GM gives the unique equal split, at which T=n/K+ng-n R_eff/4, proving the placement and budget conclusions. For the 3-by-3 torus, using the zero and nonzero eigenspace projectors of the three-cycle in each factor gives Green diagonal 2/9 and Green off-diagonals 0 and -1/18 for adjacent and diagonal sites, respectively; the example follows. The supplied verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not run. The sampled solves are corroboration, not proof of optimality over all graphs.

originality.rationale: The exact two-trap formula and its optimizer are direct specializations of a prior arbitrary-rate killed-resolvent formula in terms of the unkilled pseudoinverse, not just comparable to a one-perfect-trap result. In Jacobsen–Tien, sections 2.3 and 3.1–3.2, combine Theorems 4 and 5 at z=1. Write G=L^+, v=(kappa_a e_a+kappa_b e_b)/K, W=(I-1 v^T)G(I-v 1^T). The prior formula is (L+D)^(-1)=11^T/K+(I+WD)^(-1)W. If positivity of all rates is required, let positive rates at other sites tend to zero: L+D remains positive definite in the limit and I+WD stays nonsingular, as W is positive semidefinite and D is nonnegative. For alpha=kappa_a/K, beta=kappa_b/K and q=(beta,-alpha)^T, the trap block is W_SS=2d q q^T, W_S,: 1=-n d (alpha-beta)q, and 1^T W 1=n^2(g-2d alpha beta). Substituting these into the prior resolvent by the rank-one inverse formula gives T/n=1/K+g-2dP/K^2-d^2(1-4P/K^2)P/(K+2dP)=g+(1-d^2P)/(K+2dP). The claimed rate optimization is then immediate from monotonicity in P and AM–GM; at equal rates its resistance dependence is affine with negative slope, giving the placement rule. This is demonstrated prior implication, not a claim that the exact wording appears in the prior paper.
residual_risks: The comparison does not determine who first wrote the resulting scalar two-trap expression. A related lattice article, ScienceDirect PII S0378437118309348, was not available in full text and is not relied on for the disposition. The rejection rests on the displayed implication of the accessible Jacobsen–Tien theorems.

value.rationale: Placement and allocation of finite-rate traps are naturally motivated and the resistance form is a useful presentation. As a standalone scientific finding, however, the lifetime is mechanically obtained from the existing general absorption-resolvent theorem, and the two optimization statements reduce to strict monotonicity of one scalar rational function, AM–GM, and a linear ranking. The submitted record does not establish a distinct non-routine invariant or design principle beyond this specialization.
